title: Free AI for Excel: data analysis, formulas and charts · {name}
description: Drop an Excel file or a CSV in a browser tab and ask. A program works the numbers out, not a guess, and you get a chart or a new workbook. Free.
h1: AI for your Excel files that calculates, never guesses.
lede: Drop a workbook or a CSV in {name} and ask in your own words: which product grew, what the formula is, what changed since last month. A program works out the numbers, and you get back a chart, a table or a new workbook. Nothing to install.
cta: Try it with a sample spreadsheet

exact.title: Worked out, not guessed.
exact.why: An AI can sound sure of a total it guessed. {name} has its numbers calculated.
exact.cards: For a total, a growth or an average, the AI writes a short program and runs it on your data. The number is calculated.
On a computer in this tab
A computer in a sandbox, in the browser, never your own machine: JavaScript, and Python for data work. The first time, {name} asks before turning it on.
Each step shows as it runs. Open one to see what it was given and what came back.
where.title: Where your file goes.
where.why: There is no {name} server. What changes is the AI that answers, and you choose it.
where.cards: Your files and your tasks are kept in this browser, encrypted. Nothing reaches us.
Sent to the AI you chose
Your request and the file’s text go to the AI you picked, and nowhere else. Under every answer, {name} says where it was done.
With the AI on this computer, nothing leaves it. It needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip.
catch.items: {name} is free; the AI behind it may not be. No sign-up only with the AI on this computer.
It doesn’t run Excel macros, and a workbook with macros (.xlsm) isn’t read.
Old Excel files (.xls, from Excel 97 to 2003) aren’t read: save them as .xlsx first.
The workbooks it writes hold values and formulas. Charts come in the answer, not inside the Excel file.
{name} can be wrong. Numbers are calculated; check the words, as you would a colleague’s.
Your work lives in this browser. Clear its data without a backup and it’s gone.
faq.items: Yes, with no account at {name}. The AI that answers may want one: {free} opens a free one, or use a plan you already pay for, or the AI on this computer, with no account at all.
Yes. Say what the formula should do, in your own words: it writes it and says how it works. In a workbook it makes, formulas stay formulas, which Excel works out again.
No. A file you drop stays as it was: what {name} makes comes back as a new workbook, which you can change where it shows.
How big can the spreadsheet be?
Up to 100 MB. The AI reads a long sheet 200 rows at a time; the computer works on the whole file.
What about Google Sheets or Numbers?
Download the sheet as .xlsx or CSV, and drop that file in the box.
Does it work on a phone?
In the browser, yes. The AI on this computer needs a computer; on a phone, choose one online.
end.title: Start with the sample spreadsheet.
end.why: It opens in {name} with its question ready. Then drop your own.
